text: An n-photon protocol succeeds at a rate proportional to eta^n. Why does this make fractions-of-a-percent detector efficiency worth years of engineering?
choices: Because eta^n grows with n, so more photons are always better regardless of eta
Because at n = 20, raising eta from 0.5 to 0.98 improves the success rate by a factor of about 10^6
Because the success rate scales only linearly with eta, so small gains are minor
Because eta^n is independent of the number of photons
explanation: The exponential eta^n means at n = 20 photons, going from eta = 0.5 to 0.98 multiplies the yield by about 10^6, far more than any clock-rate gain. The scaling is exponential in n, not linear (choice 2) or independent of n (choice 3); and for eta < 1 more photons actually suppress the rate (choice 0 is backwards).
